QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_73

question.text: Nari Shakti Trust runs TWO programmes: (i) SHG-based women empowerment (SAS-400), and (ii) women-owned financial-inclusion bank accounts with micro-insurance (SAS-1300). 120 SHG women have opened first-time bank accounts. Under the cross-standard SIA engagement, the SIA should:

answer.text: Pick whichever standard the SE prefers

Assess each outcome against the applicable standard (gender indicators under SAS-400, inclusion indicators under SAS-1300); cross-reference shared beneficiaries to avoid double-counting of impact between the two standards in the aggregate Report
Combine all outcomes under SAS-100 only

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Each outcome is governed by its substantive SAS standard; the SIA must avoid double-counting the same beneficiary-outcome across both standards in the aggregate Report — e.g., 'bank account opened by SHG woman' appears under SAS-1300 as an inclusion outcome, and may influence SAS-400 'economic autonomy' separately. Cross-reference schedules are essential. **The Trap:** Option A surrenders SIA independence. Option C collapses substance. Option D shirks scope. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-standard attribution logic mirrors multi-framework reporting in BRSR (III-A / III-C Compliance) and GRI / SDG mapping. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Build a beneficiary-x-outcome matrix: rows = unique beneficiaries, columns = outcomes claimed under each standard. A single outcome per beneficiary per standard — this is the de-dup baseline.
